div.l: Ne of his techynge daungerous ne dygne
But in his speche dyscrete ⁊and benygne
To drawe folke to heuen with fayrnesse
By good ensample this was his besynesse
But it were ony persone obstynat
Whether he were of hyghe or lowe estat
Hym wolde he snybbe sharply for the nonys
A better preest I trowe nowhere none is
He wayted after no pompe ne reuerence
Ne made to hym a spyced conscyence
But cristis lore ⁊and his appostles twelue
He taught but fyrst he folowed hymselue
WYth him there was a plowman his brod
That had led of dunge many a fother
A true labourer ⁊and good was he
Lyuynge in peas ⁊and perfyt charyte
God loued he best wyth all his herte
At all tymes though he gamyd or smerte
And then his neyghbour ryght as hymselue
He wolde thresse and thereo dygge ⁊and delue
For cristis sake for euery poore wyght
Wythout hyre yf it laye in his myght
His tythes payed he bothe fayre ⁊and well
Of his propre labur and his catell
In a tabard he rode vpon a mere
There was also a reue ⁊and also a myllere
A sompnour ⁊and a pardoner also
A mancyple ⁊and myself ther was no mo
THe myllere was a stout carle for þᵉ nonys
Full bygge he was of brawne ⁊and bonys
That proued well for ouer all there he came
At wrastlynge alway he wolde haue the ram
He was short sholdred brode a thicke quarre
Ther was no dore þᵗat he nolde heue of þᵉ barre
Or breke it at rennynge wyth his hed
His berde as ony sowe or foxe was red
And therto brode as it were a spade
Vp on the cop ryght of his nose he hade
A werte and theron stode a tufte of heris
Rede as the brystylis of a sowes eris
His nostrellys black were ⁊and wyde
A swerde ⁊and a bokeler bare he by his syde
His mouth as grete was as a furneys
He was a Iangelere and a golyardeys
And þᵗat was most of synne and harlotryes
Well cowde he stele corne ⁊and tolle thryes
And that he had a thombe of golde parde
A whyt cote ⁊and a blewe hode weryd he
A bagge pype cowde he blowe and sowne
And therwyth he brought vs out of towne
A gentyll mancyple was there of the tēmple
Of whyche a catour myghte take exēmple
For to be wyse in byenge of vitayll
For whether he payde or toke by tayll
Algate he wayted so on his achate
That he was ay before ⁊and in good state
Now is it not that of god a fayr grace
That suche a lewde mannys wyte shall pace
The wysdom of an hepe of lernyd men
Of maysters had he moo than thryes ten
That were of lawe experte ⁊and curyous
Of whyche there were a dosen in that hous
Worthy to be stywardes of rente ⁊and londe
Of ony lorde that is in englonde
To make hym lyue by his owne good
In honour detles but he were wood
Other lyue scarsely as hym lyst desyre
And able for to helpe all the shyre
In ony cause that myghte falle or happe
And yet this mancyple set all ther cappe
A Reue there was a slender coleryk man
His berde was shaue as nyghe as he can
His heris were by his erys rounde y shore
His top was dockyd lyk a prest before
Full longe were his legges ⁊and full lene
Lyke a staf ther nys no calf y sene
